passage: The corridor had emptied, but Madhuri Ma'am was still at the board with a marker. Vandana hovered at the door, cheeks warm. "I didn't get the integration steps," Vandana said. "I didn't want to ask in class." "Come, sit." Ma'am redrew the graph slowly and waited each time Vandana frowned. The tea on her desk went cold. Vandana felt thankful, and a little small for needing this. "Thank you, Ma'am. I know you have to go home." "Bring me whatever you get stuck on." Vandana walked out with the notebook still open, already starting the first sum.

qa.a: Vandana had not understood the integration steps.

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling about needing help, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Thankful but a little embarrassed; the warm cheeks, the hovering at the door and the earlier reluctance to ask in class show it. 😊

qa.q: How could Vandana use the extra time well?
qa.a: Bring whatever Vandana gets stuck on, and practise sums soon after, as Vandana began doing on the way out.

qa.q: How might Madhuri Ma'am see a student who stays back to ask?
qa.a: As someone willing to learn; Ma'am stayed while the tea went cold and invited more questions.

grounding: A teacher stays after class to explain what Vandana missed; Vandana feels thankful and a little embarrassed and uses the time.

passage:
The bell rang and the Class 10 room emptied in seconds. Sachin stayed at his desk, trigonometry notebook open at a page full of crossed-out lines. Kashish ma'am was stacking papers.

"Something stuck?" she asked.

He felt his ears go red. Everyone else seemed to understand heights and distances. "Ma'am, it's fine, I'll figure it out."

She looked at the page. "That's a lot of crossing out for fine. I've got twenty minutes."

She pulled a chair beside him and drew a tower and a boy on the board, then asked him where the angle was. He got it wrong. She asked again, differently. By the third problem, he got it right on his own.

"Oh," he said. "It's just the same triangle every time."

"Every time."

When she picked up her bag, he stood too. "Thank you, ma'am. Really. Can I come on Friday with the other exercise?"

"Bring it," she said. "And bring your questions earlier next time."

qa.q: What did Kashish ma'am draw on the board?
qa.a: She drew a tower and a boy on the board.

qa.q: Why did Sachin say he would figure it out himself?
qa.a: Sachin felt embarrassed, his ears going red, because everyone else seemed to understand and he did not want to look slow.

qa.q: What did Sachin do at the end that was wise?
qa.a: Sachin thanked her clearly and asked to come back on Friday, using the offer of help instead of hiding from it.

qa.q: How might Kashish ma'am see Sachin staying back?
qa.a: She probably sees it as a good sign that he cares, and is glad to help, since she offers twenty minutes and invites his questions.

grounding: It shows a teen thankful and a little embarrassed when a teacher stays after class to explain, who says thanks and uses the time well.

"Jahnavi, you've been staring at that reaction for ten minutes," Jeevan sir said, packing his bag.

"Sorry, sir. I'll go."

"I didn't say go. I said you've been staring. What's the problem?"

"Everything after the first step." She laughed, embarrassed. "Everyone else got it in class."

"Everyone else nodded in class. That's not the same thing." He put his bag down. "Show me."

She showed him. He asked her to explain each arrow. When she got stuck, he didn't explain; he asked, "Where do the electrons want to go?" She thought. "To the oxygen?" "Why?" "Because it's… more electronegative." "Yes."

Twenty minutes later she'd done three on her own.

"Sir, you missed your bus."

"There's another."

She hesitated. "Thank you. I felt stupid asking."

"You felt stupid for five seconds. Now you know it. That's a good trade."

She wrote down three more reactions to try before Monday.

qa.q: How long had Jahnavi been staring at the reaction?
qa.a: She had been staring at that reaction for ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi feeling when she laughed and said everyone else got it?
qa.a: Jahnavi felt embarrassed and a bit stupid for needing extra help after class.

qa.q: How did Jahnavi use the time well?
qa.a: Jahnavi explained each step aloud, worked three reactions on her own and wrote down more to practise before Monday.

qa.q: How does Jeevan sir see Jahnavi asking for help?
qa.a: He sees it as a good trade, a few seconds of feeling stupid for real understanding, and is willing to miss his bus for it.

grounding: It shows a teen who feels thankful and embarrassed when a teacher stays after class, who says thanks and uses the time well.
